sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Nilesh Dave, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Hemant Sharma, learned Govt.Advocate for the re  ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C./483 of BNSS seeking regular bail by the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.259/2024 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station, Khargone, District Khargone (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable u/S 363, 366,
376, 376(2)(N), 376(3) of IPC, Section 3/4, 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and under Section 3(1)(W(ii) of SC, ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he has not committed any offence and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
It is submitted that the prosecutrix has not supported the case of prosecution in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

It is further submitted that after dismissal of first application as withdrawn the prosecutrix (PW-1), her father (PW-2) and mother (PW-3) have been examined before the trial Court, but they have completely turned hostile and not supported the case of prosecution.
It is submitted that the prosecutrix and her parents also stated that at present she is 19 years of age.
It is submitted that applicant is in custody since 20.5.2024.
Conclusion of trial will take long time.
It is, therefore, prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

5. On the other hand learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and submits that the prosecutrix has supported the case of prosecution in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.by stating that she is pregnant from the applicant.

It is further submitted that though,
the prosecutrix and her parents have not supported the case of prosecution, but the case of prosecution is supported by DNA report.
Therefore, the applicant is not entitled for bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35074 3 MCRC-47515-2024 6.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record and considering the fact that after dismissal of his earlier bail application as withdrawn, there is no change in the circumstances to consider this repeat bail application hence, this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, this repeat application for bail is dismissed.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE patil Ravindra @ Ravi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154821216/
